purpose: Explainable vendor-neutral recommendation engine for Resilience IQ. Converts assessed business requirements, current capability, risk and evidence into ranked resilience patterns and implementation guidance.
principle: Score patterns only after hard constraints and mandatory resilience controls are applied. A high assessment score must never override a requirement mismatch or critical risk.

derived_metrics.rto_gap_minutes: max(required_rto_minutes - current_rto_minutes, 0), when both are known
derived_metrics.rpo_gap_minutes: max(required_rpo_minutes - current_rpo_minutes, 0), when both are known
derived_metrics.capability_proven: current_rto_minutes != null AND current_rpo_minutes != null AND recovery_test_evidence=true
derived_metrics.strategy_mismatch: current recovery capability does not credibly meet defined business requirement
derived_metrics.evidence_gap: required control exists by assertion/design but lacks appropriate test evidence

hard_constraints.reason: Backup restoration cannot credibly satisfy sub-hour recovery without an explicitly validated exception.
Backup restore and conventional pilot-light rebuild are not credible default choices for very low RTO.
Conventional backup/restore is not a default fit for very low data-loss tolerance.
Near-zero objectives require continuously available or hot recovery architectures where technically feasible.
Cyber resilience must include protected recovery controls.
Correlated provider/failure-domain risk must be treated explicitly.
Recovery must sequence and validate shared dependencies.
Business requirements cannot be safely inferred from technology.

dimension_guidance.requirement_fit: How credibly the pattern meets required RTO, RPO and impact tolerance.
dimension_guidance.risk_reduction: Reduction of identified business, dependency, concentration and failure-domain risks.
dimension_guidance.technology_feasibility: Fit with application/data architecture, environment and constraints.
dimension_guidance.cyber_resilience: Ability to recover after compromise and preserve trustworthy recovery points.
dimension_guidance.operational_complexity: Score higher for patterns the operating model can realistically sustain; penalize unnecessary complexity.
dimension_guidance.cost_efficiency: Relative value against cost tolerance and business impact; do not optimize cost when impact tolerance is strict.
dimension_guidance.testing_evidence: Strength of existing evidence and ability to validate the proposed pattern.

pattern_fit_rules.when: required_rto_minutes >= 1440 AND required_rpo_minutes >= 1440 AND business_criticality in ['low','medium']
required_rto_minutes >= 15 AND required_rto_minutes <= 240 AND required_rpo_minutes <= 60 AND business_criticality in ['high','very_high']
required_rto_minutes <= 60 AND required_rpo_minutes <= 15 AND business_criticality in ['very_high','extreme']

explanation_template: Based on the defined business requirement, current recovery capability, dependency/cyber/concentration risk and available evidence, {preferred_pattern} is the preferred strategy because {rationale}. {alternative_pattern} remains viable if {condition}. The recommendation depends on {assumptions} and must be validated through {tests}.
guardrails: Never recommend a pattern solely because it has the highest numerical score.
Never infer RTO/RPO from existing architecture.
Never hide evidence gaps behind a high maturity score.
Never recommend active-active solely because it is technically possible.
Always provide at least one alternative unless every alternative is eliminated by a hard constraint.
Separate vendor-neutral strategy from provider implementation.
Treat cyber recovery and identity recovery as distinct from conventional DR.
Treat third-party concentration as an end-to-end resilience concern.
If critical requirements are unknown, produce a requirement-definition action rather than a false target architecture.
